intro: Some Rayong trips don't call for a beachfront resort or a rooftop pool. Sometimes you just want a clean, quiet room, a good night's sleep, somewhere safe to park, and a price that leaves cash for seafood or a ferry over to Koh Samet — IZEN Budget Hotel & Residences (Plus) is a budget hotel sitting right on Soi Plangsri off Sukhumvit Road, in the Noen Phra area of central Rayong · It's a budget-cum-serviced-residence place that sells cleanliness, quiet and an approachable price, close to Krom Luang Chumphon Shrine, Wat Pa Pradu and Yom Chinda Road, with dozens of restaurants within walking distance · There's no pool, but you get free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk and a light breakfast · From about THB 550/night, scored 8.1 (Very Good) on Trip.com and 4.3 out of 5 on TripAdvisor

body.html: Who IZEN Budget Hotel suits — to put it as simply as possible, IZEN Budget Hotel & Residences (Plus) is a hotel for people who want a "clean, quiet room on a budget" in central Rayong, without paying for a pool or a fancy lobby they won't use · It's a budget-meets-serviced-residence place on Soi Plangsri off Sukhumvit Road, in the Noen Phra–Choeng Noen area, a residential and commercial part of central Rayong rather than a beachfront tourist strip · Real reviews on Trip.com give it an overall 8.1 (Very Good) and TripAdvisor sits around 4.3 out of 5, which is solid for a hotel at this price · The people it genuinely suits are travellers who drive themselves, people in town for work or errands, couples after a quiet room that's easy on the wallet, and budget travellers using Rayong as a stop before the ferry to Koh Samet · On the flip side, if you're after a beachfront resort, a pool, a breakfast buffet or a full holiday atmosphere, this isn't the answer — it's built to be a practical place to stay rather than a plush getaway · What makes a lot of people book again is the value, the cleanliness and the location that's central yet still quiet, a combination you don't often find at a hotel starting in the low hundreds

Location and getting around — IZEN sits on Soi Plangsri, which branches off the stretch of Sukhumvit Road running through central Rayong on the Noen Phra side · The strength of the location is that it's central but tucked into a soi, so it's quieter than hotels right on the main road. Plenty of reviewers say the same thing — that it's "quiet and private" — which suits people who don't sleep well with traffic noise · Several of the city's landmarks are within walking distance — Krom Luang Chumphon Khet Udomsak Shrine is about 200 metres away, Wat Pa Pradu about 500 metres, and Yom Chinda Road (the historic street with old wooden houses and cafes) about 600 metres · TripAdvisor notes there are 36 restaurants within 500 metres and gives a walkability score of about 63 out of 100 · For longer trips, the hotel is only a few minutes' drive from central Rayong, around 10 minutes to Saeng Chan Beach and the mid-water pagoda, and about 20–25 minutes on to Ban Phe Pier for the ferry to Koh Samet · One thing worth knowing: without your own car, hailing a ride in central Rayong isn't as easy as in the bigger tourist towns, so have a ride-hailing app ready or ask the hotel about transfers in advance, because a location like this works best for people with a car

"Clean room, very quiet, easy parking, cheaper than I expected, and there's coffee and bread in the morning — for someone driving in to run errands in Rayong it's great value. I didn't need anything more than this."

Room types and decor — IZEN has several room types in a plain but practical style, with the focus on cleanliness rather than fancy decor · Every room is air-conditioned, compact in line with the budget format, and finished in light, easy-on-the-eye tones · Each room has the essentials for an overnight stay: air-con, a flat-screen TV, a fridge/minibar, a work desk and an en-suite bathroom with shower, plus toiletries and free high-speed Wi-Fi · Because the name includes "Residences," it also works for longer multi-night stays or semi-apartment stays, thanks to the fridge and the practical space for organising your own things · Many reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, and it's quiet enough to sleep soundly, which is the main draw of a place like this · But to be straight about it, there are some gripes about the rooms too — some reviewers say the rooms are fairly small, the lighting in the room and bathroom is on the dim side, and the shower in some rooms needs a bit of fiddling to get the temperature right · These are common limitations at hotels starting in the low hundreds, and they're easy to set expectations around before you book · If you want lots of light or a bigger room, it's worth asking for a larger room type or one with a window getting natural light at the time of booking

Facilities — as a budget hotel, IZEN doesn't have resort-style facilities, but it has everything you actually need for an overnight stay · The bit road-trippers love most is the free parking, which is genuinely useful in central Rayong, where many in-town hotels have limited parking · There's also a 24-hour front desk, luggage storage, a shared lounge, laundry service and free Wi-Fi throughout · Some sources mention a small fitness corner and a little coffee shop too, but this can change depending on the period and the building, so confirm directly with the hotel if it matters to you · What needs to be said clearly is that there's no pool here, which is normal for a budget hotel in town · If you want a pool, a resort over by Mae Ramphueng Beach or Saeng Chan Beach is a better fit · Overall, IZEN's facilities are built for a practical stay — arrive, park, get into your room, rest, then head out for errands or sightseeing — they're not designed for lounging in the hotel all day

Food and what's nearby — IZEN serves a light breakfast in keeping with the budget style · Plenty of real reviews agree there's coffee, bread and drinking water in the morning, which is enough to start the day before heading out for a proper meal · What helps a lot is the location, because the area within walking and short driving distance is packed with local Rayong restaurants — TripAdvisor notes there are 36 within 500 metres · If you like local food, Yom Chinda Road and Rayong's old town nearby have cafes, traditional coffee shops and made-to-order eateries · And of course, coming all the way to Rayong, fresh seafood and the town's well-known spots are a short drive away · One thing reviews mention is that the restaurant in the building or on the ground floor is closed at times, and the choice of sit-down places right outside the hotel may not be as wide as in a tourist district · For people with a car this is barely an issue, but without one it's worth planning dinner ahead or choosing a place within walking distance

Service — service is another point that draws consistent praise in real reviews · The service category on Trip.com sits around 8.2, which is high for a hotel at this price · Many guests say the staff are friendly, helpful and attentive, especially with help over parking, fast check-in and check-out, and tips on restaurants or routes around town · The 24-hour front desk makes it easier for people arriving late or leaving very early · To be straight about it, as a small budget hotel the service is simple and to the point — there are no extras like a full tour-arranging concierge or all-night room service that you'd get at a big hotel · But on sincerity and basic helpfulness, most voices say the team do well and are friendly, which matters a lot for this kind of place

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: value and the budget price are mentioned most often, the rooms are clean and well kept, the beds are comfortable and good for couples, parking is easy and free, the location is quiet and private away from the bustle of the tourist district, the staff are friendly and helpful, and the light breakfast of coffee and bread is simple but enough · On the watch-outs side: the thing mentioned most often is the shower that needs a bit of fiddling to get the temperature right, the rooms being fairly small, dim lighting in the room and bathroom, the lack of premium decor and finishes, and the limited choice of places to walk straight to in front of the hotel (the ground-floor restaurant is closed at times) · These gripes are predictable for the price, and most are fixed by setting expectations right and choosing the right room rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back

"Stayed two nights while in Rayong for work, and I was impressed by how quiet and clean it was. The room isn't big and the lighting's a touch dim, but at this price there's nothing to complain about. The staff were lovely and a big help with parking. Next time I'm in Rayong I'll stay here again."

Price and value — IZEN's starting price is about THB 550/night in normal periods, climbing to around THB 700–900 over long weekends or festivals when lots of people head into Rayong · Compared with other budget hotels in central Rayong, such as Hop Inn Rayong in a similar price range, IZEN feels very good value for the quiet and privacy, because it's in a soi rather than on the main road · What makes it genuinely worth it is getting a clean air-con room, a comfortable bed, free parking and a light breakfast for a low-hundreds price, leaving plenty of cash for seafood or a boat trip to the islands · Judged by the standard of someone who wants "a good bed on a budget" rather than "a resort experience," every baht you spend at IZEN comes back in full · But if you'll pay more for a pool, a sea view, or a newer and bigger room, you should bump the budget up and look at the beachfront resorts instead

Good to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoothly · One, this location works best for people with a car. Without one, have a ride-hailing app ready or ask the hotel in advance about getting into town and out to Ban Phe Pier · Two, if you're sensitive to low light or like a bright room, ask for a room with natural light or a larger room type at the time of booking, as some rooms are on the dim side · Three, confirm breakfast and facilities (such as the fitness corner and coffee shop) directly with the hotel, as these details can change over time · Four, there are several IZEN branches/buildings in the same area (such as IZEN Plus, IZEN Pure, IZEN Budget), so check the building name and map match your booking so you don't end up at the wrong one · Five, over long weekends and festivals lots of people head into Rayong, prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book ahead and choose free cancellation if your plans aren't set

The verdict — going by all the real reviews, IZEN Budget Hotel & Residences (Plus) is the best fit for people who want a clean, quiet room on a budget in central Rayong, especially those who drive themselves · The cleanliness, the quiet of the soi, the free parking and the low-hundreds starting price make it good value among the city's budget options · If you're looking for a beachfront resort, a pool, a breakfast buffet or a flawless new big room, this may not be the answer, and you should consider resorts over by Mae Ramphueng Beach, Saeng Chan Beach or on Koh Samet instead · But for a trip that wants "a good bed at an easy price" as a base for errands or a stopover before the ferry to the island — IZEN really does meet that need, and well, which is why so many reviewers say they'll be back

faq.q: Where is IZEN Budget Hotel & Residences (Plus) · what's within walking distance?
faq.a: The hotel is on Soi Plangsri, Sukhumvit Road, Noen Phra Subdistrict, Mueang Rayong District, central but tucked into a soi so it's quiet · Within walking distance are Krom Luang Chumphon Shrine (~200 m), Wat Pa Pradu (~500 m) and Yom Chinda Road in the old town (~600 m) · There are about 36 restaurants within 500 metres · It's around a 10-minute drive to Saeng Chan Beach and about 20–25 minutes on to Ban Phe Pier for the ferry to Koh Samet

faq.q: How much does IZEN Rayong start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 550/night for an air-conditioned Standard room in normal periods · There's a larger Superior room and a Residence type for longer stays · Prices climb to around THB 700–900 over long weekends or festivals, so book ahead and compare a few platforms first

faq.q: Does IZEN Rayong have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No pool, in keeping with the budget concept · There's a light breakfast serving coffee, bread and drinking water in the morning, which real reviews say is simple but enough · If you want a pool and sea views, consider a resort over by Mae Ramphueng Beach or Saeng Chan Beach instead

faq.q: Who is IZEN Rayong best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who drive themselves, people in town for work or errands, budget-minded couples, and people using Rayong as a stop before the ferry to Koh Samet · It sells cleanliness, the quiet of the soi, free parking and a low-hundreds price · If you're after a beachfront resort with a pool, the beach side may suit you better

faq.q: What are the parking and the quiet like at IZEN?
faq.a: There's free parking, which is genuinely useful in central Rayong, and many real reviews praise the quiet and privacy because the hotel is in a soi off the main road · Good for people who don't sleep well with traffic noise · The 24-hour front desk caters to those arriving late or leaving early

faq.q: Does IZEN Rayong have several branches · how do I book the right building?
faq.a: There are several IZEN buildings in the same area, such as IZEN Plus, IZEN Pure and IZEN Budget · When booking, check the building name and map match your booking and confirm the address with the hotel before you travel, so you don't end up at the wrong one · The main booking channels are Trip.com, Booking.com and Agoda
